change: repair the 25 CSA daily-practice articles that serve a class attribute where the Java should be (board 153)
_note_on_expect_failure: Every expect_failure below names the assertion with its [FAIL] prefix, not just its text. Without the prefix the string matches the PASS line too, so the subsumption check passes on a mutation caught by some other guard entirely. The prefix is what makes 'this guard is real' a claim rather than a hope.

checks.name: the repair deletes only what it declares, and the recovered code agrees with the article own answer key
the preflight, with a blank cell treated as an erase in every column
THE ONE THAT WOULD SHIP WRONG JAVA: the answer-key cross-check
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] a one-character change to a bound is caught
checks._why: This is the only check that can tell a repair that ate a bound from one that did not. Everything else in the suite would stay green while 25 pages taught a wrong answer, because a body with 'i <= 5' in place of 'i <= 4' is still well formed, still passes the deletion proof, and still renders perfectly.

checks.name: the stranded angle bracket has to come out with the span
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] the mangle pattern consumes the stranded angle bracket
checks._why: Drop the > from the pattern and every repaired line still begins with a stray > in front of the Java. The page would look almost right, which is exactly the failure the deletion proof exists to catch.

checks.name: strip tags first, decode second, or the check cannot see the defect it checks
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] visible() strips a real tag before it decodes an escaped one
checks._why: Decode first and the escaped <span becomes a real tag, which the next line then strips. 58 of the 200 defects vanish from the comparison written to find them and 8 articles repair 'cleanly' into bodies missing half their code. Note which assertion this trips: the obvious one, visible() on a mangled span, passes under this mutation, because with only escaped markup present the two orders happen to agree. A test about the right subject that proves nothing is the failure mode this gate exists to surface.

checks.name: the surviving well-formed spans are unwrapped, not left behind
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] a well-formed highlight span is unwrapped, text kept and tags dropped
checks._why: Leaves System.out.println with print blue and ln not, on a page with no other colour anywhere. That is the second half of what board 153 reported.

checks.name: mangling in prose must stop the sheet, not be silently skipped
checks.find: if (loose) problems.push(loose + ' mangled spans sit OUTSIDE a code block; this repair would not reach them');
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] mangling OUTSIDE a code block is refused
checks._why: A repair scoped to code blocks cannot reach prose. Without this refusal an article mangled in its question text would report a clean repair and still read wrong, with the defect count now zero.

checks.name: Java truncates integer division and JavaScript does not
checks.find: const idiv = (a, b) => { if (b === 0) refuse('division by zero'); return Math.trunc(a / b); };
checks.replace: const idiv = (a, b) => { if (b === 0) refuse('division by zero'); return a / b; };
checks._why: Day 5 asks whether (b / a == 2) holds for 7 and 3. In Java it does. Keep the remainder and the checker calls a correctly repaired article wrong, which would be a false alarm rather than a false pass, but a checker that cries wolf gets switched off.

checks.name: a for-loop variable is scoped to its loop
checks.find:
if (scopes[scopes.length - 1].has(n)) refuse('redeclared variable ' + n + ' in the same scope');
    scopes[scopes.length - 1].set(n, v);
checks.replace:
if (scopes[0].has(n)) refuse('redeclared variable ' + n + ' in the same scope');
    scopes[0].set(n, v);
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] a nested loop variable is re-declarable
checks._why: Declare into one flat scope, which is what this interpreter did first, and a nested 'for (int j ...)' is a redeclaration on the outer loop's second pass. Six of the 25 questions are nested loops, so the checker would refuse exactly the six hardest ones as unreadable and still report a clean run over the other nineteen.

checks.name: no BOM, and Matrixify reads the first column name as garbage
a SECOND implementation, in another language, scanning tags instead of substituting patterns
checks.expect: SHEET VERIFIED 25 rows, 200 mangled spans deleted
checks._why: The generator substitutes patterns. This walks each code block one tag at a time, parses each span's class attribute, and rebuilds the block from the pieces, then requires the result to be byte-identical to what the sheet carries. It imports nothing from the generator, so it cannot agree with a bug in it, and it is stricter in one place that matters: it REQUIRES the stranded > to follow each mangled span rather than assuming it. Proven not hollow by hand: change one bound in the finished sheet and it names the offset.
